# Archived references whose stored bytes are gone

**Everything here IS archived.** Each of these references has its Markdown, and
usually its PDF, published under `md/` and `pdf/`. What is missing is the
evidence behind those files: the content store no longer holds an object the
manifest names, so the archive can show the document but can no longer show what
it was made from.

That is why this is not [needs-work.md](needs-work.md). Nothing here needs
fetching before a reader can read it, and listing it as unfetched work buried
the references that genuinely have no document.

The usual cause is a scanner: the corpus is exploit research, and an antivirus
engine reads a write-up as the thing it describes. Exclude the store directory
AND the repository from the scanner before re-acquiring, or the next sweep
quietly undoes the recovery.

To work the list:

```text
refs.py check --missing-store                     # which of these still answer
refs.py acquire --missing-store --force --refetch # re-fetch the ones that do
refs.py wayback --only <url>                      # for a source that no longer does
refs.py index                                     # regenerate this file
```

A published PDF that was copied verbatim from the source's own file can restore
`raw_sha256` offline - re-import it rather than re-crawling.


1007 archived reference(s) name 1080 store object(s) that are no longer held: 54 browser_dom_sha256, 131 content_sha256, 5 landing_sha256, 2 linked_document_sha256, 880 raw_sha256, 8 translation_sha256.
